name: tadeumendonca-skills
description: The Codex carrier for this harness: one adapter registered on PreToolUse (the irreversible floor) and on UserPromptSubmit (a Codex-native preflight checking only bash, jq and the shared guard), the skill library and the MCP declaration. It REPLACES the Claude hook registry for Codex - see docs/codex-hook-bridge.md, section 18, for what that covers and what it does not. WHAT IS MEASURED, and the BUILD is part of every claim: the INSTALLED 2.0.71 carrier, its single PreToolUse registration trusted individually in the native UI, invoked PreToolUse and blocked an unquoted command-substitution fixture on Desktop 0.151.0-alpha.7.2 (default mode) and, independently, on the VS Code binary 0.154.0-alpha.6.2 (ambient permission_mode bypassPermissions), which refutes the earlier build hypothesis for the PreToolUse/Bash route. UserPromptSubmit blocking a turn was observed through a disposable native registration only; this carrier's own UserPromptSubmit registration firing after release/install is still OWED. QUOTED SUBSTITUTION: at 2.0.71 a double-quoted substitution wrapping a secret write abstained at the shared guard; the shared guard denies these measured spellings in source since #497 - not the class, and not process substitution (no adapter-side policy), and native re-verification on an installed release carrying it is OWED. NOT CLAIMED: authenticated caller identity, host/IDE shell routes, the write_stdin gap, script-content integrity, or whole-harness support. Hook trust can also be granted by an API call with NO human prompt - never treat it as a human checkpoint. TWO convenience refusals are omitted on this path (env-var prefix, redirection) because the native layer stops neither; the THIRD, command substitution, is FORWARDED because it manufactures the token every floor rule matches on - see section 15.3. Do not flatten any of this into 'whole-harness support'. RELEASES (#508): the registration resolves the adapter at call time, so a running session follows a plugin update instead of launching the deleted version; every refusal exits 2, the only code measured to block, and so does an adapter that crashes or a missing python3. The command changed in that release, so re-trust BOTH registrations after updating to it - a modified registration is SKIPPED, silently, until re-trusted. To check, run echo $(true) in a Codex session: it must be refused. See docs/codex-hook-bridge.md, section 20.
